The NYU Tandon Future Labs is the first public-private partnership with New York City tasked with creating a sustainable incubation program focused on increasing the success rate of new ventures and generating positive economic impact.

If your startup is focused on AI, digital media, clean energy, or any other world-changing tech — or if you’re a military veteran seeking to transition to civilian life as an entrepreneur — you’ll find the guidance, expertise, resources, and community you need to succeed in today’s innovation economy.
Urban Future Lab Our Urban Future Lab is New York City’s hub for smart cities, clean energy, and smart grid technology.
Veterans Future Lab Located in Brooklyn’s Sunset Park neighborhood, VFL houses early stage businesses led by military veterans and contains a prototyping space available to the public via membership.

Find more significant accomplishments on the Faculty Awards & Honors page .
Mark, generally known as the Father of Polymer Science, joined the faculty and established the Polymer Research Institute.
1945 Professor and President Ernst Weber (‘58-’69) founded the Microwave Research Institute which developed electromagnetic and microwave defense and communication systems.
1957 Eugene Kleiner (’48) helped found Fairchild Semiconductor, a pioneer in transistor and integrated-circuit manufacturing.
Kleiner later co-founded a venture capital firm that provided funding for such now-iconic companies as Amazon, Google and AOL.
1973 Renamed Polytechnic Institute of New York after encompassing the faculty, programs, and students of New York University College of Engineering.

1984 Eleanor Baum (’64) became the first female dean of an engineering school in the United States, at Pratt Institute in Brooklyn and 1995 first woman president for American Society for Engineering Education (ASEE).
2008 An affiliation is forged between Polytechnic and New York University, creating the Polytechnic Institute of NYU and paving the way for an official merger.
2009 Ursula Burns (’80) was appointed CEO of Xerox, becoming the first African-American woman ever to head a Fortune 500 company.
Turing Award from the Association for Computing Machinery for his fundamental contributions to artificial intelligence.
2014 Merger with New York University becomes official — name changes to the NYU Polytechnic School of Engineering.
2016 CSAW, the world’s biggest student-run cybersecurity event, becomes international with competitions in India, the Middle East and North Africa.

30 NEW FACULTY have joined NYU Tandon since Fall 2025 It begins with extraordinary people.
This fall, we welcomed 17 exceptional new faculty , including LaShanda Korley , a nationally recognized leader in sustainable polymer design, as Chair of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering.

They are part of a faculty distinguished not only by the caliber of their individual scholarship, but by their ambition to pursue breakthroughs that extend well beyond the boundaries of any one discipline.We are reforming our research enterprise around the solutions we are seeking.

The new Center joins the Institute for Engineering Health , the Earth Systems Institute , the NYU Quantum Institute , Urban Institute , Center for Robotics and Embodied Intelligence , and our newly unified Computer Science Department with the Courant Institute School of Mathematics, Computing, and Data Science .
Each shares a fundamental premise: the hardest problems to solve do not fit neatly within departments, disciplines, or schools, so our research enterprise cannot either.
This fall, New York City announced a $29.2 million investment in NYU’s new Quantum Fabrication Facility at NYU’s new home for Science and Technology at 770 Broadway.
Researchers, students, startups, and industry will work alongside one another, while a partnership with CUNY will create new pathways into quantum careers.
AI is becoming integral to engineering practice, so it must become integral to engineering education.

This fall, a new AI foundations course became part of our undergraduate curriculum, alongside faculty development, program-level human-centered AI strategies, and an ongoing effort to determine — with faculty and students — how these tools can strengthen learning rather than substitute for it.
